findings.issue_text: The new `OR { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` deletion branch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31 is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so the SMS cron will also delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders whose retryCount exceeds 1

`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` (lines 184, 190) writes back a value read at fetch time, so concurrent cron runs or other writers lose increments; should use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`

The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block (line 190) is unguarded; if it throws (e.g. P2025 when the row was deleted), the exception aborts processing of all remaining reminders and the route returns 500
Reminders that fail twice are hard-deleted with no log, status, or cancelled flag, making the dropped SMS unobservable; should at least log deleted IDs or mark instead of delete

The `else` branch (line 178) increments retryCount whenever `scheduledSMS` is falsy, conflating non-retryable outcomes (Twilio not configured, unverified number) with retryable failures, so permanent conditions get retried and then deleted
No tests cover the new retry/delete behavior (increment on failure, increment on caught error, deletion at retryCount > 1, non-deletion of non-SMS reminders)

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block (line 190) is unguarded; if it throws (e.g. P2025 when the row was deleted), the exception aborts processing of all remaining reminders and the route returns 500

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({...})` inside the `catch` block without its own error handling. If that update throws (e.g., Prisma `P2025` if the reminder row no longer exists due to concurrent deletion, or any DB error), the exception will escape the `catch` and abort the loop/handler, preventing remaining reminders from being processed and likely causing the API route to return a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reminders that fail twice are hard-deleted with no log, status, or cancelled flag, making the dropped SMS unobservable; should at least log deleted IDs or mark instead of delete

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the initial `deleteMany` to delete any `WorkflowReminder` where `retryCount > 1` (via an `OR` clause) with no logging or state change—just a hard delete. Since the handler increments `retryCount` on scheduling failure (both in the `else` branch and in `catch`), reminders that repeatedly fail will eventually match `retryCount > 1` and be deleted on the next run, with no record/flag indicating they were dropped. This makes those dropped reminders unobservable from the DB after deletion, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `else` branch (line 178) increments retryCount whenever `scheduledSMS` is falsy, conflating non-retryable outcomes (Twilio not configured, unverified number) with retryable failures, so permanent conditions get retried and then deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an `else` branch that increments `retryCount` when `scheduledSMS` is falsy, but it does not show what `scheduledSMS` represents or under what conditions it can be falsy (e.g., configuration missing, invalid/unverified number, intentional no-op, etc.). Without the implementation/contract of the scheduling call, it’s not verifiable from this diff that falsy results correspond to “non-retryable outcomes,” nor that this change will cause permanent conditions to be retried and then deleted. The concern is plausible but speculative given only the provided changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior (retryCount field, deletion condition, and retryCount increments), but it does not include or modify any test files. From the diff alone, we cannot verify whether tests already exist elsewhere covering this logic, nor is the absence of new tests itself a concrete defect introduced by the code changes. This finding is therefore a process/coverage concern rather than a verifiable problem in the diff.
